title: Classify 3,136 f22 decoder complements and lift all 744 survivors
body:
Among all 3,136 three-root exchanges, 2,392 fail coverage. The 744 survivors have exact minima 63 through 67 and full integer Gram witnesses at the stated modulo-four support charge.

## Scope and source

Extends #7936 for the specified single f22 loose-row class. Includes all 144 determinant-plus/minus-three cases and same-class integer lifts. Physical costs of multiples of four remain distinct. The source extension is #7869 at `06c207a9feb3994a4b987dc3010657b6e85b7956`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-decoder-three-root-integer-lifts/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. Clean replay and independent fiber/plane and integer evaluators verified the complete roster, 36,864 same-class tests, and damaged port, sign and uncorrected lift controls. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Price real integer representatives in the caller and test wider loose-row or complement families.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
